title: POST /bug-reports rejects a description shorter than 20 characters
description: bug-report.routes.js validates body('description').isString().trim().isLength({min:20, max:5000}) via express-validator before the controller runs.
preconditions: Authenticated client-panel user with a selected project
steps: POST /bug-reports with { projectId: '<valid ObjectId>', description: 'too short' } (9 chars)
expectedResult: 400 response with a validation error mentioning 'description must be 20-5000 chars'; no BugReport document is created.

title: POST /bug-reports rejects a description longer than 5000 characters and an invalid projectId
steps: POST /bug-reports with description of 5001 characters and a valid projectId
POST /bug-reports with a 25-character description but projectId: 'not-a-mongo-id'
expectedResult: Both requests return 400 with express-validator messages ('description must be 20-5000 chars' / 'projectId must be a valid ObjectId'); no document persisted for either.

title: Bug report is persisted locally with jiraStatusRaw='Sync Failed' when Jira issue creation throws, and the API still returns 201
description: createBugReport() saves the BugReport document to MongoDB before attempting jiraService.createIssue, specifically 'to prevent data loss'. If Jira creation fails (either issue.success===false or an exception), the report is updated to jiraStatusRaw='Sync Failed' but the HTTP response is still 201 with no client-visible error — the ticket is expected to self-heal via triggerBackgroundSync on the next list call.
preconditions: jiraService.createIssue mocked to reject or return { success:false }
steps: Inspect the response and then query the BugReport document directly
expectedResult: Response is 201 with success:true and the created report (no jiraKey). The persisted document has status:'Open', jiraStatusRaw:'Sync Failed', and a valid ticketNumber — the user-visible ticket is never lost due to a Jira outage.

title: Screenshot attachment failure does not fail or delay bug report creation
description: In createBugReport(), jiraService.attachScreenshot(...) is invoked without awaiting its resolution meaningfully for the response — it's a fire-and-forget call with only a .catch(logger.warn). A slow or failing Jira attachments API must not add latency to the create response or roll back the created ticket.
preconditions: jiraService.attachScreenshot mocked to reject after a 10s delay
steps: POST /bug-reports with a valid description and a small PNG screenshotBase64
Measure response time and response status
expectedResult: Response returns 201 well under the attachment mock's 10s delay; the ticket and its jiraKey are present regardless of the eventual attachment failure, which is only recorded via a warn-level log.

title: GET /bug-reports (My Tickets) filters strictly by organizationId AND userId
description: listMyBugReports builds filter { organizationId, userId: req.userId } — two different users in the same org and project must never see each other's reports in this endpoint.
preconditions: User A and User B in the same org each have 1 bug report
expectedResult: User A's response contains only User A's report; User B's response contains only User B's report — neither list includes the other's ticket.

title: GET /bug-reports/all is blocked by requirePermission('bug-report.read_all') at the route level
description: bug-report.routes.js gates /all with requirePermission('bug-report.read_all') before listAllBugReports runs, independent of any UI tab visibility logic.
steps: As a normal user (no bug-report.read_all), call GET /bug-reports/all directly
expectedResult: Request is rejected with 403 before listAllBugReports executes — no cross-user report data is returned even if the frontend tab were bypassed.

title: POST /:id/sync creates the missing Jira ticket on demand and surfaces a 500 if that also fails
description: syncBugReportStatus(): when report.jiraKey is absent it attempts jiraService.createIssue right away (unlike the fire-and-forget background path) and, unlike createBugReport, throws AppError.internal if this synchronous attempt also fails — giving the caller an explicit signal rather than silently marking 'Sync Failed' again.
preconditions: A BugReport with jiraStatusRaw:'Sync Failed' and no jiraKey
steps: POST /bug-reports/:id/sync with jiraService.createIssue mocked to succeed
Repeat against a second report with jiraService.createIssue mocked to fail
expectedResult: First call returns 200 with the report now carrying jiraKey/jiraId/jiraUrl and jiraStatusRaw:'Open', and triggers a 'bugReportCreated' email. Second call returns 500 'Failed to create Jira ticket: <reason>' and the report remains without a jiraKey.

title: POST /:id/comments returns 400 when the ticket has no jiraKey yet
description: addComment() explicitly checks `if (!report.jiraKey) throw AppError.badRequest('Jira ticket not synced yet. Cannot post comments.')` — comments can only be relayed to a real Jira issue.
preconditions: A BugReport with jiraStatusRaw:'Sync Failed' / no jiraKey
steps: POST /bug-reports/:id/comments with { comment: 'Any update?' } against the unsynced report
expectedResult: 400 response with message 'Jira ticket not synced yet. Cannot post comments.' — no call is made to jiraService.addComment.
